One should mix camphor, kaṅkola, cloves, betel nut, nutmeg, ginger, sugar-candy, and betel leaves with lime powder, the heartwood of khadira, and a powder of musk and sandalwood. (1)
They say this betel leaf is excellent; it bestows good fortune and grants beauty and happiness.
It increases health, intellect, memory, and wisdom, and it also acts as a stimulant for the digestive fire. // 2 //
They declare this to be the preeminent state among the states that kindle the bodiless one; for from this, indeed, [all things arise].
(Ap 100) Therefore, all [things...]
Happy people enjoy that which brings joy day and night. // 3 //
Betel leaves remove wind; the areca nut destroys excessive salivation caused by phlegm;
the lime powder subdues phlegm and wind; and the heartwood of the khadira tree powerfully destroys bile.
For thus they describe betel as a remedy for even the three types of defects;
therefore, a wise man—even an ordinary person—should partake of it in some measure. 5.
Now follow those things to be avoided, with the exception of betel.

Physicians do not recommend betel for eye diseases, nor for internal hemorrhaging, nor for wounds, nor for indigestion, nor for poisoning, nor for consumption; nor in cases of alcoholism, nor for delusion, fainting, or asthma. (5)
Now follows the rule for the proper time for betel.
After eating food, drinking water, and consuming a large meal,
a person should wait for one ghaṭikā before chewing betel leaf.
(Āyurveda-prakāśa 101) Now, the qualities of nutmeg (*jātīphala*).
It pacifies wind and phlegm, is beneficial for the heart, stimulates the digestive fire, removes bad taste from the mouth, and instantly digests what has been eaten. (7)
Jatiphala is digestive, stimulates the digestive fire, removes phlegm, and cures throat ailments;
it is excellent for excessive salivation and destroys indigestion.
And this is wholesome. // 8 //
Kalikā is digestive, appetizing, and extremely cooling in its post-digestive effect;
it destroys wind, bile, and phlegm, and it cures fever and vomiting. (9)
Now, the qualities of *elā*.
The two types of cardamom (elā) are beneficial in cases of vomiting, dysuria, intoxication, and loss of appetite.
Now, the qualities of nutmeg (jātipatrī):
Jātipatrī is sweet, very cooling, and sweet in its post-digestive effect; it also cures loss of appetite.
Now follows the rule for the duration of time required for the ripening of betel nuts.
Those who know the matter declare that betel nut fit for use as *tāmbūla* is [fully developed] after three months;
when the month has passed, they become complete, exceedingly pleasing, and captivating to the mind. (11)
(Ap 102) Now, the specific qualities of various types of *kramuka* betel nuts and *tāmbūla* leaves.
The large betel nut (kramuka) increases phlegm and promotes worms;
at its end, that which begins with the color white increases phlegm and destroys worms.
Now, the qualities of camphor.

Sharp and hot, yet extremely cooling in its post-digestive effect, it removes itching and urinary disorders, stops nasal discharge and tears, destroys worms, and conquers thirst, dyspnea, and cough. It subdues phlegm, cures throat obstructions, and overcomes numbness of the tongue.
Camphor indeed possesses the quality of a fragrant luster and cures bile-related diseases; crystal is [of the same nature].
Camphor destroys throat-seizure, numbness of the tongue, various nasal discharges, excessive secretions, phlegm, urinary disorders, and worms; it is another [remedy] for the eyes.
It destroys urinary disorders, thirst, and burning sensations, and increases fortune and good luck. // 16 //
Now, the qualities of musk:
Musk is rich in fragrance, possesses a pungent taste, and is alkaline, bitter, and astringent;
it removes grief and flatulence, subdues phlegm and wind, increases bile, and is beneficial for the eyes.
It is a cause of mental exhilaration, destroys the effects of irregular poisons, toxins, and artificial poisons, and eliminates bodily foul odors.
It thoroughly pacifies hunger, thirst, and the provocation of bile, as well as impotence, wasting, and poison. // 17 //
Now follows the section on ointments.
Sandalwood destroys blood-bile (raktapitta), removes burning sensations, fainting, and diarrhea;
it is cooling, increases phlegm (śleṣman), is pleasing to the heart, and slightly aggravates wind (vāta). // 18 //
It always removes bile and blood, alleviates burning sensations, and when consumed regularly, it pacifies fainting, delusion, thirst, and poisons, while destroying foul odors.
It clearly cuts away itching, skin diseases, fistula-in-ano, and exhaustion; it overcomes fainting, urinary disorders, and dysuria, and constantly destroys hemorrhoids. (19)
The fragrant [incense], which is the refuge of liberation, always dispels the various arrays of diseases.
The Malaya mountain [wind] destroys the defect of delusion, subdues hemorrhagic fever (raktapitta), alleviates fainting and wasting, and eliminates foul breath from the mouth. // 20 //
It is cooling, destroys bile, is sweet with a slight bitter taste, removes itching, swelling, and poison, kills worms, bestows good fortune and luster,
produces an indescribable fragrance on the limbs, and grants nourishment.

Sandalwood or saffron, which produces supreme contentment in the mind, is smooth and allays thirst; they are to be applied according to the season, while the application of musk and camphor is to be used at all times.
There is a profusion of flower-garlands from the season of passion, abundant camphor powder, and pure white garments suitable for use at all times. // 22 //
Thus ends the chapter on unguents in the Great Ocean of Ayurveda composed by Suṣeṇa.
Now, therefore, the qualities of garments are described.
Pure white silk cloth pacifies kapha and vāta; however, those who know declare that thread or this garment pacifies all three doṣas. // 1 //
A very white silk garment (*dukūla*) here bestows strength, pacifies bile, increases vitality and luster, provides pleasure, and cuts through the burning pain of the vital organs (*marmans*).
Linens are purifying, dispel thirst and defects, provide stability, bestow luster, increase phlegm, are exceedingly pleasant when white, pure, and destroy diseases caused by bile. // 2 //

Māñjiṣṭha is heating, causes a burning sensation, alleviates kapha, and is wholesome; it constantly brings about the excellent destruction of wind-disorders (vātāmaya) and conquers the provocation of phlegm (śleṣmaprakopa).
It is hot, counteracts cold, removes impurities, and dispels both phlegm and wind.
He always wears garments dyed with madder, which remove the illusion of ignorance. // 3 //
Thus ends the chapter on garments in the *Āyurvedamahodadhi* composed by Suṣeṇa.
This work composed by Suṣeṇa is completed.
May this be an offering to the glorious Sāmbasadāśiva.
May there be auspiciousness!
Homage to the illustrious Sarasvatī.
